**Setup.** A fold matching two points is the perpendicular bisector of the segment joining them. Reflecting across that line sends one point to the other.

**Fold line.** The segment from $(1,3)$ to $(5,1)$ has midpoint $(3,2)$ and direction $(4,-2)$, so the normal is $n=(2,-1)$. The fold line is
$$2(x-3)-(y-2)=0 \iff 2x-y-4=0.$$

**Check.** Let $f(x,y)=2x-y-4$. Then $f(1,3)=-5$, and reflecting gives
$$(1,3)-\frac{2f}{|n|^2}\,n=(1,3)+\frac{10}{5}(2,-1)=(5,1),$$
which confirms the fold line.

**Reflect $(8,4)$.** Here $f(8,4)=16-4-4=8$, so
$$(p,q)=(8,4)-\frac{2\cdot 8}{5}(2,-1)=\left(8-\tfrac{32}{5},\;4+\tfrac{16}{5}\right)=\left(\tfrac{8}{5},\;\tfrac{36}{5}\right).$$

**Verify.** The midpoint of $(8,4)$ and $(1.6,7.2)$ is $(4.8,5.6)$, and $2(4.8)-5.6=4$, so it lies on the fold line. The displacement $(-6.4,3.2)$ is parallel to $n$, so the fold is perpendicular to the segment as required.

**Result.** $p+q=\tfrac{8}{5}+\tfrac{36}{5}=\tfrac{44}{5}=8.8$.

This value does not match any of the listed choices (9.2, 9.3, $9.\overline{3}$, 9.4, 9.5). The computation checks out under the stated fold, so either the problem statement or the answer choices appear to have a transcription error. The original problem I recall used $(0,2)\mapsto(4,0)$ and $(7,3)\mapsto(p,q)$, which may be the intended version; I have not verified that variant here.

Final answer: $p+q = 44/5 = 8.8$, which is not among the choices (A)–(E).
